sink: mineflayer 4.35.0 node_modules/mineflayer/lib/plugins/chat.js chatWithHeader(): `if (!header && message.startsWith('/')) { bot._client.chat(message); return }`, which reaches node_modules/minecraft-protocol/src/client/chat.js _signedChat(): `if (message.startsWith('/')) { const command = message.slice(1); ...; client.write('chat_command'/'chat_command_signed', { command, ... }); return }` - a real server chat_command packet, not a chat message
dep_evidence: mineflayer 4.35.0 and minecraft-protocol 1.64.0, both installed under node_modules/, read directly - neither guards against a leading '/'; that behavior is their documented intended feature for player-driven clients
why: message: z.string() has no length/content/prefix restriction. Verified myself by reading the exact installed mineflayer/minecraft-protocol source: any message starting with '/' is silently converted from a chat message into a real chat_command packet sent with the bot's own permissions. If the bot account has elevated in-game permissions (common for automation bots), any caller of send-chat can execute arbitrary server commands (/op, /gamemode, /ban, /stop, etc.) merely by prefixing the message argument with '/', with zero mediation in this repo's own code.
